tasks.title: The Transition from Monks to Lay Painters in Medieval Europe
paras: Before the eleventh century most painters in Europe were monks (members of a religious group that lives in seclusion) and their work was exclusively religious. Such artists worked in a variety of art forms, including metalwork and manuscript illumination (the art of illustrating handwritten books), and they did not sign their work, as art was considered an opportunity for religious meditation not self-advancement. Between the eleventh and the fourteenth centuries, however, painting began being practiced by lay professionals, who had no connection to religious institutions. Inevitably, this had consequences both for working practices and for the art that was produced. These new painters followed a trade like any other. Like the woodworker, the potter, the baker and the weaver, the lay painter offered his technical proficiency for fee. He was by no means above asking the baker for use of his ovens to make charcoal, employed as a black pigment. Nor would the artist sneer at the cook, with whom he had many skills in common.

One of the consequences of this transition from monk to artisan was increasing specialization. Painters were painters, not to be confused with illuminators, dyers, or workers in wood and metal. Such distinctions were rigidly enforced by the guilds—powerful associations of workers within specific trades—that developed to safeguard the employment of tradespeople against competition and economic uncertainty, so that it would have been unthinkable for a painter to be called in to illuminate a book page.

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes the central theme of the passages?

options.A: Medieval guilds restricted artistic freedom by enforcing rigid specialization.
options.B: The shift from monastic to secular painters transformed art into a trade and spurred professional specialization.
options.C: Lay painters relied on collaborations with bakers and cooks due to limited technical skills.
options.D: Anonymous religious art declined as painters prioritized self-advancement over meditation.

questions.analysis: 题型：主旨题 原文分析：身份转型（首段核心）： 前僧侣时期：画家是隐修团体成员，创作目的为宗教冥想，作品匿名且跨领域（金属工艺、手抄本彩绘）。 世俗化时期：画家成为独立职业者，通过技术变现谋生（"offered his technical proficiency for fee"），与木匠、陶工等平级，体现艺术从神圣仪式向市场交易的转变。 选项分析： A. 中世纪行会通过僵化分工限制艺术自由 错误点：夸大了行会的“限制”属性，忽略其作为专业化结果的历史合理性。 文本反证：行会的职能是“保障从业者就业”（safeguard employment），其分工机制是职业化转型的必然产物，而非主动压制艺术自由。 C. 世俗画家因技术缺陷需与面包师合作 错误点：曲解协作关系。画家借用烤炉制炭（"asking the baker for use of his ovens"）体现跨行业资源整合，而非技术不足。 文本反证：明确提到画家与厨师“共享技能”（"many skills in common"），证明其技术熟练度足以胜任多元任务。 D. 匿名宗教艺术因画家追求名利而衰落 错误点：虚构因果关系。世俗画家的核心动机是谋生（"followed a trade like any other"），非追逐个人声誉；文本未提及“匿名传统消失”，仅强调僧侣时代不署名的宗教属性。

questions.stem: The word "proficiency" in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 题型：词汇题。 选项分析： 题干词proficiency意思为“熟练、精通”，和B项“技巧、技能”意思最接近。A项意为“帮助”，C项意为“监管”， D项意为 “创造”均和题干词意思不符。

questions.stem: Paragraph 1 supports all of the following statements about painting before the eleventh century in Europe EXCEPT:

options.A: Painting was mostly done by monks.
options.C: Paintings did not include the names of their creators.
options.D: Painting limited the time that painters had for religious meditation.

questions.analysis: 题型：否定事实信息题。 原文分析：A和B选项对应原文第一句Before the eleventh century most painters in Europe were monks (members of a religious group that lives in seclusion) and their work was exclusively religious. C选项对应原文 they did not sign their work；D选项的religious meditation在原文有，但是没有提到绘画会减少画家用来宗教冥思的时间。

questions.stem: Paragraph 1 suggests which of the following about the social status of the first lay painters as compared to that of other tradespeople?

options.A: Painters were often looked down on by other tradespeople.
options.B: Painters were considered equals to other tradespeople.
options.C: Painters had higher status than cooks, but lower status than woodworkers and potters.
options.D: Painters were considered equal to monks and thus of higher status than other tradespeople.

questions.analysis: 题型：推断题。 原文分析：根据题干可以定位到倒数第四和第三句话These new painters followed a trade like any other. Like the woodworker, the potter, the baker and the weaver, the lay painter offered his technical proficiency for fee.意思是这些早期的画家从事的工作和其他行业的人是一样的，没有区别，所以推断他们的社会地位也是差不多的，对应B选项。

questions.stem: Which of the sentences below best expresses the essential information in the highlighted sentence in the passage? Incorrect choices change the meaning in important ways or leave out essential information.

options.A: Despite the rigid distinctions enforced by the guilds to safeguard the employment of tradespeople, painters could be called in to illuminate book pages.
options.B: It would have been unthinkable for guilds to develop without safeguarding the employment of painters who illuminated book pages.
options.C: Distinctions developed among guilds in the way that the guilds safeguarded the employment of tradespeople against competition and economic uncertainty.
options.D: The guilds, which safeguarded tradespeople against competition and economic uncertainty rigidly enforced distinctions among tradespeople.

questions.analysis: 题型：句子简化题。 原文分析：原句的句子主干是 Such distinctions were rigidly enforced by the guild that developed to safeguard the employment of tradespeople against competition and economic uncertainty.（这种区别由行会严格执行，其发展目的是为了保障商人的就业免受竞争和经济不确定性的影响）。D选项把原句的被动语态改成主动，但是重要信息都是对应的。A选项中despite这个让步逻辑是原文中没有的；B和C选项的主干和原句不符，故排除。
